newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin recovering, but out of public view.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin recovering, but out of public view.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin made steady progress on Saturday, four days after his quintuple heart bypass operation, but kept out of public view.
A Kremlin statement said he was being more active in his suite in the Central Clinical Hospital and his blood pressure, pulse and temperature were all stable for the third day.
"Four days after the operation, the patient is moving around significantly more," it said.
Yeltsin, fretting to be back at his Kremlin desk, moved to the familiar Central hospital on Friday from the Cardiology Research Centre where he had seven hours of surgery on Tuesday.

Chief surgeon Renat Akchurin suggested on Friday that the 65-year-old president might be ready to appear in public on Saturday. The Kremlin said however it knew nothing of any plans for Yeltsin to make any television appearance.
Yeltsin has been visited by members of his family and briefed in person on the state of the nation by Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais.
Yeltsin's wife Naina joined Chernomyrdin and Chubais on Saturday in giving a Kremlin reception for the doctors who assisted in the operation.
Eminent U.S. cardiologist Michael DeBakey and two German specialists on post-operative complications acted as consultants.

Yeltsin has issued several decrees and statements from his hospital room. The latest, made public on Saturday, congratulated the Russian interior ministry on annual Police Day and hailed its battle with crime.

His four-month absence from the helm of this nation of 150 millions has led to a build-up of potentially destabilising problems, among them widespread discontent in the armed forces and a huge backlog in wage payments across the country.
It has also seen a Kremlin power struggle resulting in the sacking of army-general-turned-politician Alexander Lebed and the continuing rise of free-market champion Chubais.
But Yeltsin's rapid recovery so far indicates he will soon be back at his desk with renewed energy, now his heart is receiving a proper supply of blood for the first time in years.
Akchurin, speaking on NTV television, said Yeltsin was recovering ahead of schedule.
"I think that somewhere around 10 to 12 days after the operation he could quite easily fulfil the major part of his duties," he said.
Yeltsin's press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said the president had requested recordings of his favourite classical composers -- Mozart, Vivaldi and Tchaikovsky.
"I think that when a man who is recovering asks for his favourite music, that is the best sign of his return to health," Yastrzhembsky told NTV on Friday evening.
"The patient is walking around the ward and eats three meals a day alone and unaided," Yastrzhembsky added.
Some Russians saw Naina Yeltsin's new haircut as another sign of confidence. According to one tradition, it is bad luck to shave or cut your hair while a member of your family is in danger.
